title: improv·artist · fluid (Helen Frankenthaler)
mutation_directive: improv artist: fluid via Helen Frankenthaler

improv_extras.practice: soak-stain; thinned pigment soaks the canvas; geological flow

v1.feedback: Strong Frankenthaler read — the asymmetric four-pool composition with lobular edge perturbation and gravity-settle genuinely evokes soak-stain, and the CSS canvas-grain overlay is a smart contextual touch. To push further: the pools currently spread as independent islands; adding a thin chromatographic bleed where overlapping pools mix colors (blend vCol in the fragment shader where alpha contributions overlap, perhaps via an additive pre-pass or soft depth test) would capture Frankenthaler's signature — pigment layers reading through each other. The breathing oscillation post-soak (0.015 * sin) is nearly invisible; consider instead a slow capillary creep that keeps advancing edges at 1/10th the initial rate so the piece never fully settles, rewarding sustained watching.

v2.feedback: The chromatographic bleed between pools and lobular edge modulation are faithful to Frankenthaler's capillary wicking, and the palette is genuinely restrained. Two refinements: the top-down orthographic-style view makes the pools read as flat colored blobs rather than geological stain — consider a slight oblique camera angle (camera.position.set(0, 10, 5)) so the subtle y-displacement from depth becomes visible and the pools gain dimensionality. Second, the slow creep is lovely but the initial soak (exp(-t*0.32)) saturates within ~8 seconds leaving a mostly static image; adding a very slow second-stage chromatographic separation where edge particles drift outward and shift hue slightly would sustain the feeling of pigment still traveling through fiber.
